article_title: DuckDB 1.5.6 Ships Correctness and Crash Fixes, and Previews a Windows Build of v2.0 That Ran TPC-H More Than 6x Faster

content_preview.title: DuckDB 1.5.6 Ships Correctness and Crash Fixes, and Previews a Windows Build of v2.0 That Ran TPC-H More Than 6x Faster
content_preview.summary: DuckDB's sixth 1.5 patch release fixes wrong-result and crash bugs; the team also reports a v2.0.0-dev Windows build finishing a TPC-H SF300 run in 129 seconds versus 822.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The DuckDB team released version 1.5.6 on September 28, 2026. According to the [DuckDB blog](https://duckdb.org/2026/09/28/announcing-duckdb-156.html), it is the sixth patch release in the 1.5 (Variegata) line and ships bugfixes, performance improvements and security patches. The same post gives an early Windows benchmark of the upcoming v2.0.0-dev, which the team says was more than 6x faster than v1.5.6 on a TPC-H workload.

editor_notes.content_quality: Concise Briefing (534 words, within the 300-800 range). Clear structure: Overview, What Is in 1.5.6, Windows Preview of v2.0, What We Don't Know, Context. The benchmark is properly scoped as vendor-run, single-machine, Windows-only, and dev-build.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both snapshots from disk via gunzip (manifest sha256 present, status 200, no archive fallback, suspicious_patterns null for both). source-0.html.gz (duckdb.org/2026/09/28/announcing-duckdb-156.html): dated 2026-09-28; 'the sixth patch release in DuckDB's 1.5 (Variegata) line'; 'ships bugfixes, performance improvements and security patches'. Correctness list confirmed verbatim in substance: #24240 LIMIT pushdown through volatile projection with OFFSET, #24239 filters on volatile groups through aggregates, #24119 UNNEST pushdown, #24399/#24551 Top-N window elimination NULLs, #25831 common subplan elimination with UNION ALL arms sharing a join subtree, #25714 silent truncation of long integer literals into HUGEINT, #25766 max on Hive partition column after file pruning, #25728 TIME_NS in Parquet, #26162 Parquet VARIANT shredding. Crashes: #25103 Top-N with LIMIT 0, #24427 url_decode with TRY() on dictionary-encoded columns segfault, #24447 failed checkpoint marker recovery, #25490 close main WAL handle before renaming over it during WAL recovery. Misc: #26102 enable_optimistic_write, #25283 harden temporary file reads, #25214 always quote identifiers in error messages, #24362 unify C API symbol versioning and stabilize all v1 APIs. Benchmark section: Windows 11 25H2, laptop, 128 GB RAM, 12 AMD Ryzen AI 300 cores with SMT (24 threads), TPC-H SF300, each query run twice on v1.5.6 and v2.0.0-dev (alpha43586); 'The total runtime for DuckDB v1.5.6 was 822 seconds, while for v2.0.0-dev it was 129 seconds. That's more than 6× faster!'; attribution to 'a switch to the clang-cl compiler and a new allocator'; caveat 'please do not expect a 6× speedup to generalize to all workloads – but rest assured that you should see significant improvements'; 'v2.0.0 in October'. All quotes verbatim. 822/129 = 6.37, so the 'more than 6x' claim holds arithmetically. source-1.html.gz (github.com/duckdb/duckdb/releases/tag/v1.5.6): 'released this 28 Sep', 'This is a bug fix release'; confirms #25103 (Top-N LIMIT 0 crash), #25490 (WAL handle), #24447 (listed as 'backport 24260', the checkpoint-marker fix is only identified by the blog title), 'Backport DuckDB 2.0 API spellings to 1.5' (#24852), 'Bump DuckLake for v1.5.6', 'bump iceberg'. All GitHub-attributed claims supported.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All specifics (fix list, hardware, dataset, alpha build id, timings, date Sept 28, October target) trace to the two cited sources. The 129s vs 822s numbers match the blog. The article correctly says the result is a single vendor-run benchmark and that no independent replication appears in sources reviewed. Minor omission: the article does not state that per-query hot (second-run) times were used; not a factual error.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral. The blog's promotional phrasing ('blew our minds') is not adopted; the team's own caveat is reproduced faithfully. The headline states the benchmark result as an event in the past tense and mentions the Windows dev build.
editor_notes.originality: New topic: the 1.5.6 patch release and the Windows benchmark. The only prior DuckDB coverage is the 2026-08-20 v2.0 Cyanoptera preview (different subject); the cross-reference /article/2026-08/20-duckdb-previews-v20-cyanoptera-replacing-its-postgres-derived-parser-with-a-peg-grammar-ahead-of-a-fall-release resolves to an existing article and uses the correct singular /article/ form.
concerns: Both sources are DuckDB-owned (duckdb.org blog and the GitHub release page) with no independent secondary source; the article discloses this and frames the benchmark as vendor-reported. duckdb.org and github.com are both on config/source_allowlist.txt.

The GitHub release notes list the checkpoint-marker fix only as 'backport 24260 ... #24447' without a descriptive title, so that item is confirmed by the blog, not by the GitHub page; the article attributes it to the blog, so this is consistent.
recommendations: Where available, add an independent replication or secondary coverage of the benchmark in follow-ups.
Note that reported timings are hot (second-run) totals.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-scoped Briefing. Headline number, caveat, hardware, dates and fix descriptions all verified against the on-disk snapshots. No suspicious patterns. Approved for publication as-is.
